content: Diabetic foot ulcers are a significant complication of diabetes, often resulting from abnormal pressure distribution on the foot. Pressure-relieving treatments are commonly employed to promote healing of these ulcers, but the most effective method remains uncertain. A systematic review was conducted to evaluate the impact of various pressure-relieving interventions on the healing of diabetic foot ulcers. The review included randomized controlled trials and involved a comprehensive search of multiple databases up to November 2012, without restrictions on language or publication status. Data from eligible studies were independently extracted and analyzed by two reviewers. Fourteen trials, involving a total of 709 participants, met the inclusion criteria. One study compared two types of non-removable casts but found no significant difference in their effectiveness. Seven studies, with 366 participants, compared non-removable casts to removable pressure-relieving devices. In five of these studies, non-removable casts were associated with a statistically significant increase in the number of healed ulcers compared to removable devices (relative risk [RR] 1.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01 to 1.36, P = 0.04). Two studies, involving 98 participants, demonstrated that non-removable casts were significantly more effective in healing ulcers compared to dressings alone. Additionally, one study investigated the combination of Achilles tendon lengthening with a non-removable cast. This approach resulted in a significantly higher number of healed ulcers at seven months compared to using a non-removable cast alone (RR 2.23, 95% CI 1.32 to 3.76). Furthermore, ulcers in this group were more likely to remain healed at two years (RR 3.41, 95% CI 1.42 to 8.18). Other interventions, such as surgical debridement, felt padding applied to the foot, and felted foam dressings, did not show statistically significant benefits in promoting ulcer healing. In conclusion, non-removable pressure-relieving casts are more effective than removable devices or dressings alone in healing diabetic plantar foot ulcers. Moreover, combining non-removable casts with Achilles tendon lengthening appears to enhance healing outcomes in certain cases, such as forefoot ulcers.
